recipes.name: German Potato Salad
ingredients_raw: 4 medium potatoes, cut into bite-sized pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes; cook until fork-tender, 8 to 15 minutes. Drain.

While potatoes are cooking, cook bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until browned and crispy, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove bacon to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving drippings in the skillet. Chop or crumble bacon when cool enough to handle.

Add sugar and flour to drippings in the skillet, then pour in water and vinegar. Cook over medium heat, stirring any browned bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon, until dressing is thick, 3 to 5 minutes. Turn off heat.
Add potatoes, crumbled bacon, and green onions to the skillet; stir until coated. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: German Potato Salad
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for German potato salad has a tangy bacon vinaigrette and can be served at any temperature — perfect for potlucks, picnics, and barbecues.

video.description: Featuring buttery tender potatoes and crispy bacon tossed in a tangy vinaigrette, German potato salad is a next-level side dish that differs quite a bit from its American counterpart. Put the mayo aside for this recipe and opt for a unique gravy-meets-salad-dressing that sets this dish apart from the rest. With a few simple ingredients, German potato salad delivers a burst of flavor that will be a hit at every summer picnic and barbecue. Plus, it can be served at any temperature, so no need to haul the cooler around!

review.reviewBody: I grew up eating german potato salad and this was excellent, however, I like to add more vinegar and more water as the potatoes love to soak up the liquid. Try heating up the leftovers in a skillet and you'll be in for a real taste treat!

I tripled this recipe for a family gathering, cooking the potatoes the night before and refrigerating them. I cut the sugar in half, used chicken broth instead of water, added a little more vinegar, and used yellow onions instead of green. My bacon was lean, so it wasn't too greasy. Once it was done, I transferred it to a slow cooker to keep it warm. Delicious! I'd make it again.

This so close to the recipe handed down from my German grandmother. My grandma’s uses more white vinegar, a teaspoon of celery seed, and a yellow onion instead of the green. It’s part of a full German spread (with jagerschnitzel, spaetzel, and cucumber salad) so I like to make the potato salad a day ahead - just leave out the bacon. I prefer this hot, so reheat at 275 for 45 min then stir in the bacon just before serving. It’s my favorite part of the meal.

Very good recipe, in the main, but depending on the type of potatoes you use, and how thick you like the "dressing" you may want to cut back on the flour a bit. I used eight potatoes for our group, but kept the tablespoon of flour, which I found to be a bit too much. I at least doubled the water, and used a combination of cider and white wine vinegar. There was a brightness to the white wine vinegar which surpassed the organic cider vinegar I had. Which surprised me a bit. I also added a bit of garlic (I love it in most stuff), and substituted sliced yellow onion and parsley for the green onions/scallions, which I didn't have. And that was great. I also added a bit more bacon fat (which I keep in reserve in my freezer), which was necessary for the quantity of potatoes I used. I salted the water to cook the potatoes liberally, but you still need to salt fairly heavily to get some flavor into the spuds. I had suggestions from various folks while I was making it (always fun!) to add some whole grain mustard, which I elected not to do. 

Also, this same recipe but without the flour yields a brighter, tarter version, which I tend to prefer personally, but my family LOVED the thicker dressing!

WE LOVE THIS RECIPE AS IS but the next few times I made it I added our "personal" touches. I quadrupled the recipe as I have a BIG eaten family. I used red potatoes (large and small), boiled whole with skins for approx. 15 minute (took each one out when tender) let them cool then sliced in quarters. Used 24 oz. of "Smokey" bacon (chopped in small pieces prior to frying), used 1 large chopped sweet onion (use less next time) and sautéed in bacon grease after bacon removed. Used a bit less sugar, raw apple cider vinegar (more), veggie stock/broth instead of water (more when needed), added celery seed, dry mustard, some chopped up dill pickle and juice, and added fresh parsley at the end (all for personal preference). I cook everything on stove top in a huge frying pan, fry bacon, remove, add chopped onion, and then add flour etc..... tweak as I'm making, as we LOVE LOTS OF FLAVOR!!!! The salad tastes MUCH BETTER the next day and so on! We love German Potato Salad!!!This recipe is AWESOME AS IS, tweak to your desire~ THANK YOU & Bon Appétit

I really liked this recipe. I made only a few changes for my taste. I tried it with one tablespoon of sugar because I like more tang than sweetness. Next time, I will omit it entirely. I used white balsamic vinegar, but I am sure it is just as good with white wine vinegar. I added some chopped celery to the green onion and cooked them in the bacon grease along with the sugar, flour, vinegar and water. That it just because I wanted them soft like the potatoes. And I also added more vinegar and water because I agree with another reviewer that the potatoes soak up a lot of liquid. And don't be shy with salt and pepper. The salt helps to enhance the bacon flavor.

Slight Modifications for my taste. I steamed sliced, 8 small Redskin and 4 med sized Gold Potatos for 15 minutes on Med-HI and I used 1/3 cup of White Wine Vinegar and added two tea spoons of salt and a teaspoon of black pepper. I used 1/4 lb of Smoked Bacon, I used dried chives because I did not have fresh on hand. But I tell you. It came out wonderful. Like MY German Mother made it before she turned into an Organic Green Smoothie Sucker. Love you though. Great Recipe, I love it.

Be sure not to over cook the potatoes, they need to be a little firm so they won’t turn to mush when added to the other ingredients. If they are soft enough for mashing, that’s TOO soft. They still taste yummy, but they are tastier when not cooked to that level. Great recipe!

This was Really good. I steamed russets whole then peeled the skin off while they were warm but cool enough to handle. Doubled the sauce, but found it too sweet for my taste. Hubby loved it. I used apple cider vinegar which maybe added to the sweetness, too. Would make again with white vinegar and no sugar.

Good basic recipe. I had to change it a little bit, because when I got my green onions out, they had gone bad, so I used part of a sweet Walla-Walla onion instead, and sauteed it in the bacon grease after taking the bacon out. I also used white balsamic vinegar, which added a little more sweetness. I used 2 extra bacon slices too, but took out some of the grease. The dressing got really thick; not sure if it was supposed to or not, but it stuck to the potatoes this way which I thought was good. Since I didn't have the green onions I used about a TBS. of dried chives for color. I also used red unpeeled potatoes. Had this with grilled sausages on wheat rolls and fresh corn on the cob. Very good!
It has great flavor but needs more liquid. Soaks it up real fast. Will make it again.
So delicious, this is going to be a winter regular on our menu.
100% German, need to add some pickles, fresh peas and boiled eggs!!!
Absolutely delicious. I did make it twice and the second time I used pickled jalapenos and the pickle juice from them. If you like a little spice - it truly was yummy!

Just picked up a 10lb bag of potatoes and looking for recipes. My dear aunt used to make this each time we got together and I just loved it as a kid. From what I remember, the potatoes are sliced, not cubed. Very helpful suggestions in the review section. I'll definitely be doubling up on the liquids cuz I like my potato salads on the moist side. And of course, more bacon!
Try with triple sauce, double potatoes, bacon etc Fresh parsley, green onions, s&p
My 11-year-old is a picky eater but declared this to be delicious. (The rest of us did, too!) I've never cared for potato salad, but this recipe is :chef's kiss:
